questions.prompt: For the API server, how should long-running research runs be executed/managed in the MVP?

options.text: Async runs executed in-process; POST returns runId; poll for status (single-node MVP)
Synchronous request: POST blocks until completion (simple but fragile)
Queue-based workers with Redis (e.g., BullMQ) from day one
Split API + worker processes with DB-backed leasing (no Redis)

answers.notes: this should be as production grade as we can make it. so let's make sure we have the ability to recover on errors/restarts of the process and are giving meaningful status updates on each job from a status endpoint. should be able to configure how many concurrent jobs are supported (the rest are queued) and an admin interface (web or command line is fine) that lists ALL jobs and allows the admin of the system to cancel, reprioritize jobs, etc. (normal users would never see this or know it exists)

answers.notes: actually YES.. this is perfect.. then we can set rate limits and quality thresholds per user. first X searches are high quality, but if that user goes beyond downgrade them to cheaper models/search harness until month end to help control costs. but do it on a per user basis so those who aren't abusing are still getting full benefit.
